content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the causes and consequences of kidney failure
Evaluate dialysis and kidney transplant as treatments
occurs when the kidneys can no longer adequately filter blood. Without treatment, waste products accumulate and become toxic. Two main treatments exist:
When kidneys cannot adequately perform their functions
Artificial filtering of blood when kidneys fail
Fistula (joined artery and vein) in arm
Connected to blood vessels and bladder
Original kidneys usually left in place
Also suppress immune response to pathogens
It's not as effective as healthy kidneys
Kidney transplant means dialysis is never needed again
Blood type and tissue matching are essential
Dialysis is only for elderly patients
Kidney failure can occur at any age
When kidneys cannot adequately filter blood
Allows some substances through but not others
Kidney failure: kidneys cannot filter blood adequately
Causes: diabetes, high blood pressure, infections
Consequences: urea build-up, water retention, electrolyte imbalance
Dialysis filters blood artificially using semi-permeable membrane
Peritoneal: uses abdomen lining, done at home
Transplant: donor kidney, better quality of life
Rejection prevented by tissue matching and immunosuppressants
Both treatments have advantages and disadvantages
